sources.name: Ourednik historical-basemaps

coverage.temporal: Local imported snapshots: -4000 to 2010; modern handoff 2020

limitations: Work in progress with mixed source provenance. Precision ordinal 1/2/3 is approximate/moderate/legal, not measured positional error. Cultures can overlap.

Local importer holds each snapshot until the next, joins names across one missing snapshot, groups dependencies by ruler and attaches modern countries by name. These are software heuristics, not source-backed lifetimes.
No interpolation of shapes or invention of earlier/later polygons.
sources.nextAction: Pin upstream commit and feature identifiers; preserve source snapshotYear separately from display interval. Audit names and dependency relations before using inherited dates.

sources.name: ETH CShapes 2.0

coverage.temporalModel: country-period rows with separate year/month/day fields

limitations: 2018 PDF discusses 2017 endpoint; current file and changelog extend to 2019.

Coding manual: de jure changes; excludes changes below 10000 sq km, some unrecognized secessions, temporary wartime changes; may backdate current lines when evidence is absent. Some January dates are placeholders.
Downloaded GeoJSON lacks status/ruledby/b_def fields described in manual. Historical colonial rows exist but sovereignty cannot be inferred from names alone.
String timestamps differ from component date fields by hours/day: retain both and use date components for reviewed normalization.
sources.nextAction: First integrate reviewed Sudan/South Sudan transition as a paired replacement with exact-date handling. Fetch table formats to recover dependency metadata before broader import.

sources.name: ETH CShapes-Europe

coverage.spatial: European extract with selected North African and transcontinental entities
coverage.temporalModel: integer From/To years; not global daily schema

limitations: Endpoint/schema differ from global product. Do not assume 1806 minimum means complete 1806 coverage.
Observed Belgium 1886-1919 and 1886-2023 rows overlap. Blind import is blocked until duplicates/alternative histories are explained.
Year transitions cannot establish exact treaty days. Same geometry or small coastline differences may be source resolution changes, not territorial change.
sources.nextAction: Use exact Denmark extraction as technical pilot, then review 1864/1920 changes and source interval conventions. Crosswalk Germany/Prussia and Austria phases explicitly; defer transcontinental entities.

limitations: Centennial snapshots cannot establish annual transitions. Northern Europe above 60N excluded.

sources.nextAction: Inspect public 1500 demo shapefile metadata and footprint, then select missing European snapshot coverage. No purchase or contact made.

sources.name: World Historical Gazetteer

coverage.temporal: dataset and place-specific; no universal start/end

limitations: Main site returned 403; documentation accessible. Most API endpoints require token.
Geometry can be a point and dates can describe habitation, not state control. Do not create borders from city points or name matches.
sources.nextAction: Use /reconcile batches then /entity/{type}:{id}/api for identifiers and citations; exact-match and period review required. Polygon-only datasets need their own inventories.

pipeline: Pin source URL, retrieval date, version and SHA256; keep original bytes outside runtime.
Validate schema, coordinate CRS/order, rings, finite values, topology and overlaps; never auto-repair without a record.
Separate source observation dates, source validity, identity lifetime and display interval.
Crosswalk each source ID and dated phase to reviewed entity IDs; preserve dependency holder and sovereignty distinctly.
Retain uncertainty and disputed/claimed/control semantics; do not interpolate unknown polygons.
Generate staged exact-geometry samples with immutable provenance; independent historical and geometry review.
Convert reviewed polygons to shared-arc TopoJSON; measure distortion and retain raw sources; lazy-load regional date slices.
Integrate neighboring changed polygons together and test transition dates, BCE semantics, antimeridian, taps and mobile payload.
